artist.name: Sody
artist.short_description: Sody — an Afterglow editorial selection for listeners exploring emotional pop.
artist.biography: Sody is the stage name of British singer-songwriter Sophie Dyson. In an original interview, she discussed growing up in a large family and writing songs from an unusually young age. Her catalogue developed through singles such as ‘Maybe It Was Me’, ‘What We Had’ and ‘Bedroom Ceiling’. She has also collaborated with Cavetown on ‘is your bedroom ceiling bored?’, while the song ‘fools (can't help falling in love)’ includes her contributions alongside Foster and Sarcastic Sounds. The 2020 EP real growth takes time was presented as a personal collection, with Sody specifically describing ‘butterfly’ as addressing mental health. In 2025, she released her debut album THE HELL OF APRIL and characterized it as an account of heartbreak rather than a completed healing journey. That personal framing makes her catalogue especially suitable for careful, sourced song discussions. For Afterglow, she occupies an intimate, confessional corner of emotional pop. This is an editorial description of her work, and the artist's explanation for one track should never be applied automatically to another.
